response: No, reimplantation of spinal cord arteries during thoracic and thoracoabdominal aneurysm repair is not a waste of time. In fact, it is a crucial step in minimizing the risk of spinal cord injury, which can lead to paralysis or other neurological deficits. Reimplanting these arteries helps to preserve blood flow to the spinal cord, reducing the risk of ischemia and subsequent damage. This technique is considered an important aspect of spinal cord protection strategies in these complex surgical procedures.
